subject: Geography
description: Major plateaus of the world by location and features

questions.stem: The 'Tibetan Plateau' — the highest and largest plateau in the world — lies chiefly in:

options.option_text: India
China (Tibet)
Nepal
Bhutan

questions.explanation: Tibetan Plateau — also called the 'Roof of the World' — average elevation > 4,500 m; area ~2.5 million km². Mostly in China's Tibet Autonomous Region and Qinghai Province. Extends into Ladakh (India) and small parts of Bhutan and Nepal. Source of major Asian rivers — Indus, Brahmaputra, Ganges (via tributaries), Yangtze, Mekong, Yellow River.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'Deccan Plateau' of peninsular India is bordered by:

options.option_text: Himalayas on the north
Satpura hills on the north, Western and Eastern Ghats on the sides
Aravallis on all sides
Vindhyas on the south

questions.explanation: Deccan Plateau — roughly triangular. Northern edge — Satpura hills (with the Vindhyas just beyond, north of Narmada). Western edge — Western Ghats (rising up from the Arabian Sea coast). Eastern edge — Eastern Ghats (lower, more broken). The plateau tilts gently eastward — which is why major peninsular rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) flow east to the Bay of Bengal.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'Colorado Plateau' — famous for the Grand Canyon — lies in:

options.option_text: Canada
United States
Mexico
Brazil

questions.explanation: Colorado Plateau — in the southwestern USA, covering parts of Utah, Arizona, Colorado and New Mexico. Average elevation ~2,000 m. The Colorado River has carved the Grand Canyon (~1.6 km deep) across this plateau over 5-6 million years. Other famous US landmarks here — Monument Valley, Bryce Canyon, Zion, Mesa Verde.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Match the plateau with the continent where it lies. A. Ethiopian Highlands. B. Brazilian. C. Anatolian. D. Australian. List-II: 1. Africa, 2. South America, 3. Asia, 4. Oceania/Australia.
questions.explanation: Ethiopian Highlands (Africa) — source of the Blue Nile. Brazilian Plateau (S. America) — covers much of central/eastern Brazil. Anatolian Plateau (Asia) — covers most of Turkey. Australian Plateau / Western Plateau (Oceania). Other big ones — Iranian (Asia), Bolivian / Altiplano (S. America), African Plateau south of the Sahara.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Chota Nagpur plateau is a major source of minerals in India — especially:

options.option_text: Petroleum and natural gas
Coal and iron ore
Gold and silver
Uranium and thorium only

questions.explanation: Chota Nagpur Plateau (Jharkhand, parts of Chhattisgarh, Odisha, WB) — India's 'mineral storehouse'. Coal (Jharia, Bokaro, Giridih); iron ore (Jharkhand/Odisha); bauxite; copper; mica. Ranchi and Jamshedpur are major industrial cities here. The Damodar river (Bengal's 'sorrow' before the Damodar Valley Corporation dams) flows through it. Petroleum is chiefly offshore (Mumbai High) and in Assam.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'Altiplano' — the vast, arid highland plateau in South America — is in:

options.option_text: Argentina and Chile
Bolivia and Peru
Brazil and Colombia
Venezuela and Guyana

questions.explanation: Altiplano — 'high plain' — lies in western Bolivia and southern Peru, in the Andes. Second-highest plateau in the world after Tibet. Contains Lake Titicaca (world's highest navigable lake, ~3,812 m) and Uyuni salt flat (world's largest salt pan, rich in lithium). Capitals La Paz (Bolivia) and Puno (Peru) sit on the Altiplano.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: A plateau formed by extensive lava flows is called a:

options.option_text: Piedmont plateau
Volcanic (lava) plateau
Continental plateau
Intermontane plateau

questions.explanation: Volcanic / lava plateaus form when lava flows from many fissures cover a large area and solidify. Example — Deccan Traps (India) — huge lava plateau laid down ~65 million years ago, some theories linking it to the K-Pg mass extinction; Columbia River Plateau (USA); Drakensberg in Ethiopia. Piedmont plateau — 'at the foot of mountains' (e.g., near the Appalachians). Intermontane — between mountains (e.g., Tibet, between Himalayas and Kunlun).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'Meseta Central' — a vast elevated tableland averaging 600–700 m above sea level — forms the broad interior heartland of which European country?

options.option_text: Spain, where it forms the wide interior plateau of the country
France, where it lies between the Massif Central and the Pyrenees
Italy, occupying the Po Valley and the central Apennine highlands
Portugal, stretching from the Tagus estuary to the Douro valley

questions.explanation: The Meseta Central is Spain's defining landform — a broad, largely flat plateau that dominates the country's interior. France's equivalent highland is the Massif Central, which is a different feature entirely; Portugal shares a small western fringe of the Meseta but is not the country it 'forms the heartland of'.

questions.stem: The 'Patagonian Plateau' — a cold, wind-swept tableland lying south of the Río Colorado river — belongs almost entirely to which South American country?

options.option_text: Chile, along the Pacific coast south of the Atacama desert
Bolivia, in the southern Andes between Potosí and Tarija
Argentina, between the Andes foothills and the Atlantic coast
Brazil, in the southern region bordering Uruguay and Paraguay

questions.explanation: Patagonia — including the Patagonian Plateau — lies almost entirely within Argentina, stretching from the Andean foothills eastward to the Atlantic. Chile controls only a narrow Pacific coastal strip. Bolivia is landlocked further north, and Brazil's southern border does not extend to this plateau.

questions.stem: The 'Potwar Plateau' in northern Pakistan is of great significance to palaeontologists worldwide primarily because it has yielded:

options.option_text: Rich copper, chromite, and bauxite ore deposits of Precambrian age
Fossil remains of Sivapithecus and diverse Miocene-era Siwalik fauna
The world's largest recoverable rock salt deposits at Khewra mine
Evidence of the oldest-known Bronze Age metallurgical workshops in Asia

questions.explanation: The Potwar Plateau and the adjoining Siwalik Hills have yielded fossils of Sivapithecus (a Miocene hominoid considered ancestral to the orang-utan lineage) along with a rich Siwalik fauna — making it a globally important palaeontological site. The Khewra salt mine (option C) is nearby in the Salt Range but is an economic, not fossil, resource.

questions.stem: The 'Loess Plateau' of north-central China owes its distinctive yellow, fine-grained, deeply gullied terrain primarily to:

options.option_text: Alluvial deposition by the Yangtze River and its tributaries over millions of years
Wind-blown (aeolian) fine silt transported from the Gobi and Central Asian deserts
Volcanic ash accumulations from repeated eruptions along the Pacific Ring of Fire
Glacial outwash deposits left behind after Pleistocene ice sheets retreated northward

questions.explanation: Loess is wind-blown (aeolian) silt — carried by westerly winds from the Gobi Desert and arid Central Asian basins and deposited over millions of years to form the Loess Plateau. The Yellow River (Huang He), not the Yangtze, drains through it and carries its silt load to the sea, giving it the characteristic yellow colour.

questions.stem: In geomorphology, a plateau that lies completely or largely enclosed between converging mountain ranges on multiple sides — as the Tibetan Plateau is enclosed by the Himalayas and Kunlun — is specifically classified as:

options.option_text: A piedmont plateau, formed at the base of an eroding mountain range
A continental plateau, rising steeply and abruptly from surrounding lowlands
An intermontane plateau, enclosed on multiple sides by mountain belts
A dissected plateau, carved into ridges by extensive river and stream erosion

questions.explanation: An intermontane plateau (inter = between, montane = mountains) is flanked by mountain ranges on several sides — the Tibetan Plateau, Bolivian Altiplano, and Iranian Plateau are classic examples. A piedmont plateau lies at a mountain's foot on one side only; a continental plateau (e.g., Antarctic Ice Sheet) rises sharply from open plains; a dissected plateau is defined by erosion, not mountain enclosure.

questions.stem: The 'Anatolian Plateau' of central Turkey undergoes sustained westward 'tectonic escape' — moving as a coherent block toward the Aegean — because it is being squeezed between which two converging plates?

options.option_text: The African Plate advancing from the south and the Aegean subplate from the west
The Arabian Plate pushing northward and the Eurasian Plate resisting from the north
The Indo-Australian Plate from the east and the Adriatic microplate from the northwest
The Somali Plate from the south and the Iranian microplate from the southeast

questions.explanation: Arabia has been colliding with Eurasia since the Miocene (after the closure of the Tethys Sea), generating compression across the Middle East. With nowhere to go vertically, the Anatolian block escapes westward along the North Anatolian Fault (NAF) and East Anatolian Fault (EAF) — the classic 'tectonic escape' model. The African Plate subducts under the Aegean but is not the primary driver of Anatolia's westward motion.

questions.stem: The 'Guiana Highlands' of South America are dotted with ancient sandstone tabletop mountains called 'tepuis'. Angel Falls — the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall at 979 m — plunges from which tepui?

options.option_text: Mount Roraima, the triple-border tepui shared by Venezuela, Guyana, and Brazil
Chimantá Massif, the largest tepui complex in Venezuela's Gran Sabana region
Cerro de la Neblina, the highest tepui on the Brazilian-Venezuelan border at 2,994 m
Auyán-tepui, also called Devil's Mountain, in Bolívar State, Venezuela

questions.explanation: Angel Falls (Salto Ángel / Kerepakupai Merú) drops off the edge of Auyán-tepui in Venezuela's Canaima National Park — named after aviator Jimmy Angel who flew over it in 1933. Mount Roraima is the most famous tepui but has no comparable waterfall; Cerro de la Neblina is the highest peak but lies on the border; Chimantá is the largest tepui system but not the source of Angel Falls.
